title: Derived composition preserves the specified adjunction normalization
statement:
Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], with ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $L_a:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$, $L_b:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, and $L_c:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$ be exact additive functors, with specified additive right adjoints $R_a,R_b,R_c$. Fix a natural isomorphism $\lambda:L_bL_a\xrightarrow{\sim}L_c$, and let $\kappa:R_c\xrightarrow{\sim}R_aR_b$ be its conjugate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] under $L_c\dashv R_c$ and the composite adjunction $L_bL_a\dashv R_aR_b$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. For an additive functor $H$ write $C(H)$ for termwise application to complexes, and write $D(H)$ for its descent when $H$ is exact. A complex $I$ is K-injective if every chain map from an acyclic complex to $I$ is null-homotopic. Compute total right derived functors $\mathbf R R_i$ on K-injective resolutions [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], and use the adjunctions $D(L_i)\dashv\mathbf R R_i$ induced by the specified underived adjunctions: the canonical derived adjunctions of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors], where $D(L_i)$ is the left derived functor of the exact functor $L_i$.

There is a natural isomorphism $\kappa^D:\mathbf R R_c\xrightarrow{\sim}(\mathbf R R_a)(\mathbf R R_b)$ with the following normalization: at a K-injective $I$ of $\mathcal C$, it is the class of $C(\kappa)_I:C(R_c)I\to C(R_a)C(R_b)I$ under the canonical resolution identifications (in particular $C(R_b)I$ is K-injective). This $\kappa^D$ is precisely the conjugate of $D(\lambda):D(L_b)D(L_a)\xrightarrow{\sim}D(L_c)$ under the derived adjunction for $c$ and the composite of the derived adjunctions for $a,b$. Thus after these comparisons the unit and counit are exactly the composite unit and counit, not arbitrary adjunction structures on isomorphic functors.

proof.text: Write $Q$ for localization, with its category understood from the argument, and suppress the canonical termwise composition identifications. By [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories], the three Grothendieck abelian categories have K-injective resolutions. For each $i=a,b,c$, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] applies to the specified $L_i\dashv R_i$: additivity is assumed and $L_i$ is exact. Thus $C(R_i)$ preserves K-injectives. In particular, for K-injective $I$ in $\mathcal C$, both $C(R_b)I$ and $C(R_c)I$ are K-injective, as is $C(R_a)C(R_b)I$. Let $\beta_{i,J}:Q C(R_i)J\to\mathbf R R_i(QJ)$ be the derived-functor comparison of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; it is an isomorphism when $J$ is K-injective.

Let $a_i$ be the hom bijection on homotopy categories supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], and $\Phi_i$ the specified derived hom bijection, the canonical bijection of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors]. Its normalization at a K-injective $J$ is
$$\Phi_i(Qf)=\beta_{i,J}\circ Q(a_i(f)),\qquad f:C(L_i)X\to J.$$
Here and below $f$ may denote a homotopy class. To check the hypotheses and formula in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general], take its right functor to be $R_i$ and its left functor to be $L_i$. For a quasi-isomorphism $s:J\to J'$, [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives a unique homotopy class $t:J'\to J$ with $ts=1$: lift $(Qs)^{-1}$ using its bijection and use injectivity to check $ts=1$. Thus $1_J$ is final in the outgoing quasi-isomorphism category. The right diagram is essentially constant with value $Q C(R_i)J$, identified with $\mathbf R R_i(QJ)$ by $\beta_{i,J}$. On the left, exactness makes every $Q C(L_i)(P\to X)$ an isomorphism, so their inverses give the representing cone with value $D(L_i)(QX)$. The cited lemma's formula with $s=1_J$, $t=1_X$ gives the display. Every derived map $D(L_i)(QX)\to QJ$ has a unique homotopy representative by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], so this computes the entire hom bijection, not merely selected chain maps. These are precisely the induced adjunctions, with no change of unit or counit.

proof.text: Put $L^D_{ba}=D(L_b)D(L_a)$, $R^D_{ab}=(\mathbf R R_a)(\mathbf R R_b)$ and $\lambda^D=D(\lambda)$. Exactness permits termwise descent of $\lambda$ and its inverse by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Use the composite derived adjunction $L^D_{ba}\dashv R^D_{ab}$ of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Define $\kappa^D$ to be the conjugate of $\lambda^D:L^D_{ba}\to D(L_c)$ under this adjunction and the specified adjunction for $c$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], it is a natural isomorphism; its inverse is the conjugate of $(\lambda^D)^{-1}$. It remains to prove the asserted representative formula for this particular isomorphism.

proof.text:
For K-injective $I$ set
$$\gamma_I=(\mathbf R R_a)(\beta_{b,I})\circ\beta_{a,C(R_b)I}:Q C(R_a)C(R_b)I\xrightarrow{\sim}R^D_{ab}(QI).$$
Both factors are isomorphisms by step 1. If $w:C(L_b)C(L_a)X\to I$, apply step 2 first for $b$ and then for $a$, whose target $C(R_b)I$ is K-injective. Naturality of $\Phi_a$ in its target gives
$$\Phi_{ba}(Qw)=\gamma_I\circ Q\bigl(a_a(a_b(w))\bigr).$$
This uses exactly the composite hom bijection of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]: the first transposition gives $\beta_{b,I}Q(a_b(w))$, and the second gives $(\mathbf R R_a)(\beta_{b,I})\beta_{a,C(R_b)I}Q(a_a(a_b(w)))$. Thus the comparison $\gamma_I$ records both resolution identifications, including application of $\mathbf R R_a$ to the inner identification.

source.place: Tags 0DVC/0FND, pre-derived adjunction hom formula applied twice; categories.tex Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits

proof.text:
Let $\varepsilon^0_c$ be the counit on complexes and set $u=\varepsilon^0_{c,I}\circ C(\lambda)_{C(R_c)I}$. The conjugate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate], together with the termwise adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy], says
$$a_a(a_b(u))=[C(\kappa)_I].$$
Indeed, this is the composite-adjunction transpose of $\varepsilon^0_{c,I}C(\lambda)_{C(R_c)I}$; the termwise unit and counit in that transpose are exactly those defining $\kappa$. Step 2 for $c$, applied to $\varepsilon^0_{c,I}$, gives $\Phi_c(Q\varepsilon^0_{c,I})=\beta_{c,I}$ by the triangle identity. Equivalently,
$$\varepsilon^D_{c,QI}\circ D(L_c)(\beta_{c,I})=Q\varepsilon^0_{c,I}.$$
By the defining conjugate formula and naturality of the composite hom bijection in its source, transposing $Qu$ therefore gives $\kappa^D_{QI}\beta_{c,I}$. Step 4 gives the same transpose as $\gamma_I Q(C(\kappa)_I)$. Cancel $\beta_{c,I}$ to obtain
$$\gamma_I^{-1}\circ\kappa^D_{QI}\circ\beta_{c,I}=Q(C(\kappa)_I).$$
This is the required representative, with precisely the canonical resolution comparisons.

source.place: Tags 0FND/0DVC and 09T5, derived adjunction normalized by the termwise counit; the explicit conjugate evaluation supplies the normalization in sites-cohomology.tex Tag 0D6E

proof.text:
Every complex $K$ admits a quasi-isomorphism $s:K\to I$ with $I$ K-injective by step 1. Naturality of the already constructed $\kappa^D$ gives
$$\kappa^D_{QK}=R^D_{ab}(Qs)^{-1}\circ\kappa^D_{QI}\circ(\mathbf R R_c)(Qs).$$
These are the canonical resolution identifications of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], so step 5 also identifies the comparison computed on any resolution and makes it independent of that choice. Finally the definition of conjugation [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] equates the hom bijection for $c$, followed by $\kappa^D$, with precomposition by $\lambda^D$ followed by the composite hom bijection. Taking identity morphisms in these bijections gives
$$R^D_{ab}(\lambda^D_X)\circ\eta^D_{ba,X}=\kappa^D_{D(L_c)X}\circ\eta^D_{c,X},\qquad
\varepsilon^D_{ba,Y}\circ L^D_{ba}(\kappa^D_Y)=\varepsilon^D_{c,Y}\circ\lambda^D_{(\mathbf R R_c)Y}.$$
The composite unit and counit here are exactly those of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. These equations prove the claimed normalization of both adjunction structures.
